en: Paṭṭhānapakaraṇa:
Dhammānulomapaccanīya (3), Dukapaṭṭhānapāḷi (2) 14.37.
Saraṇaduka (The Pair on Having a Refuge)
Dependent on a state that is a refuge, a state that is not a refuge arises by way of the root condition.

Dependent on a state that is a refuge, a state that is not a non-conflict arises by way of the root condition. Dependent on a state that is a refuge, states that are both not a refuge and not a non-conflict arise by way of the root condition.
Dependent on a state that is without conflict (*araṇa*), a state that is not without conflict arises by way of the root condition (*hetupaccaya*).
Dependent on states both with conflict (*saraṇa*) and without conflict, a state that is not with conflict arises by way of the root condition.

There are five [conditions] in the case of the root; two in the case of the object (*ārammaṇa*) … pe … one in the case of the result (*vipāka*) … pe … five in the case of non-disappearance (*avigata*).
In the Negative (Paccanīya) section on Non-root (Nahetu):
Dependent on a state that is with-conflict (*saraṇa*), a state without-conflict (*naaraṇa*) arises by way of the non-root condition (*nahetupaccayā*).
Dependent on a state that is without conflict (*araṇa*), a state that is not without conflict arises by way of the not-root condition. (Abbreviated.

Under the not-root condition there are two; under the not-object condition, three; under the not-predominance condition, five … pe … under the not-prenascence condition, four … pe … under the not-kamma condition, two … pe … under the not-nutriment, not-faculty, not-jhāna, and not-path conditions, one … pe … under the not-dissociation condition, two … pe … under the not-disappearance condition, three.
(The co-nascence section, the condition section, the dependence section, the conjoined section, and the associated section should also be expanded in the same manner as the dependent section.)
A state with a protector (saraṇa) is a condition, by way of root-condition, for a state without a protector (na-saraṇa).

A state with a protector is a condition, by way of root-condition, for a state without conflict (na-āraṇa). A state with a protector is a condition, by way of root-condition, for a state that is both without a protector and without conflict.
A state that is without conflict (*araṇa*) is a condition for a state that is not without conflict by way of the root-condition (*hetu-paccaya*).

A state with conflict (*saraṇa*) is a condition for a state that is not without conflict by way of the object-condition (*ārammaṇa-paccaya*). A state with conflict is a condition for a state that is without conflict by way of the object-condition. (Abbreviated.

There are four [types of condition] in the case of the root, four in the case of the object, five in the case of the predominance, four in the case of the immediate, ... pe ... four in the case of the conascent.

Five [conditions] in the mutual [condition], two in the dependence [condition], seven in the decisive support [condition], four in the strong support [condition], two each in the prenascence, postnascence,

and repetition [conditions], four in the kamma [condition], one in the resultant [condition], [and so on for] nutriment … path [conditions], two in the association [condition], three in the dissociation [condition] … non-disappearance [condition], seven.

A state that is with-conflict (*saraṇa*) is a condition for a state that is without-conflict (*nasaṇa*) by way of object-condition (*ārammaṇapaccaya*), co-nascence-condition (*sahajātapaccaya*), decisive-support-condition (*upanissayapaccaya*), post-nascence-condition (*pacchājātapaccaya*), and kamma-condition (*kammapaccaya*).

A state that is with-conflict is a condition for a state that is without-conflict by way of object-condition, co-nascence-condition, and decisive-support-condition. (Abbreviated. [In the negative analysis:
seven [conditions] are excluded by not-root; seven by not-object; seven by not-predominance; seven by not-proximity …pe… seven by not-co-nascence.

Five [conditions] do not exist in relation to the mutual condition when there is no dependence; five ... pe ... six in relation to the prenascence condition ... pe ... five in relation to the association condition;
four in relation to the dissociation condition ... pe ... four in relation to the non-disappearance condition.
With the root condition as the basis, there are four in relation to the object condition. (Abbreviated.)
With not-root condition, four [answers] for the object [condition]. (Abbreviated.
(It should be expanded in the same way as the section on questions in the Wholesome Triplet.)
